quote: Systems that consolidate records into extracted facts or abstractions (Chhikara et al., 2025; Ye et al., 2026) are compact but give up accuracy: the details they discard are gone for good, and consolidation can make a memory faulty even when it is distilled from useful experience (Zhang et al., 2026a).
reason: Explains why existing consolidation-based memory systems sacrifice accuracy and cannot recover discarded details.

quote: Recent studies separate user-centric memory, which personalizes an agent to its user, from agent-centric memory, which accumulates the agent’s own experience, and they find that the two face reversed challenges (Huang et al., 2026b,c).
reason: Distinguishes user-centric and agent-centric memory and explains why a unified system must address conflicting requirements.

quote: We present MIRIX-2.0, a multi-agent memory system designed to be practical, accurate, and efficient at once.
reason: Core thesis and primary contribution statement of the paper.

quote: To the best of our knowledge, MIRIX-2.0 is the first memory system that handles both user-centric and agent-centric memory, serving personalization and the refinement of agent skills from one store.
reason: Highlights the novel unified architecture supporting both user personalization and procedural agent skill refinement.

quote: Six memory agents under a Meta Memory Manager write complete records to a typed evidence plane in a vector database, the system of record, so details survive consolidation and every graph fact the answer receives cites the rows it came from.
reason: Describes the foundational storage-versus-index separation and provenance guarantee of MIRIX-2.0.

quote: Two mentions of the same dated event therefore share one frame, while two undated events with similar wording, such as two runs on different days, stay separate.
reason: Explains the temporal occurrence identity rule that prevents distinct episodic events from collapsing.

quote: MIRIX-2.0 treats retrieval as the construction of a bounded evidence set rather than as open-ended similarity search.
reason: Captures the core design principle behind graph-owned retrieval under explicit budgets.

quote: Semantic Dream never rewrites the memories in the vector database, and it consolidates neither episodic-only anchors nor fact nodes.
reason: Specifies how semantic AutoDream performs lossless structural merges without mutating stored evidence.

quote: It judges each finished task session from quotes in its transcript, distills lessons worth reusing and mistakes worth avoiding, and lets a curator (Zhang et al., 2026c) create or edit skills whose edits can cite the experiences behind them.
reason: Details the procedural AutoDream refinement pipeline from task transcripts to cited skills.

quote: It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, where it leads the strongest baseline by 14.3 points, and with AutoDream disabled it gains 31.0 and 22.0 points over HyperMem on single-hop and multi-hop document QA.
reason: Key quantitative results on conversational recall and document QA benchmarks.

quote: As procedural memory, it yields the highest mean success among the compared memory methods on ALFWorld and WebShop and reaches 49.2% on MetaClaw-Bench, against 44.0% for MetaClaw’s skill library.
reason: Key quantitative results demonstrating procedural memory effectiveness across interactive agent benchmarks.

quote: On LoCoMo, graph retrieval raises overall accuracy from 85.7% for M0 to 88.4% for M1, and semantic AutoDream raises it to 91.4% for M2.
reason: Ablation result isolating the accuracy gains of the provenance hypergraph and semantic AutoDream.

quote: Organizing explicit evidence does not by itself guarantee the inference needed to resolve a detective question.
reason: Identifies an accuracy boundary observed on DetectiveQA where M1 trails baselines.

quote: Relative to M0, M1 increases ingestion time by 3.8 to 4.0 times across the three document tasks.
reason: Quantifies the ingestion-time overhead introduced by hypergraph construction on long documents.

quote: The full system with AutoDream is not timed, and the retrieval bounds cover the evidence a question inspects, not latency measured as the history grows.
reason: States key evaluation boundaries regarding unmeasured M2 latency and scaling of wall-clock latency with history length.
